name: influenza-crossparadigm
title: Blueprint to pipeline to three substrates: one backend-neutral blueprint, run faithfully on CPM, vertex and center-based, with a pluggable subcellular layer
description:
This investigation covers the `viva-multicell-blueprint` pipeline end to end: the
backend-neutral blueprint (a versioned, statically validated artifact), the single
`blueprint_pipeline` composite that compiles it onto a mechanics backend, the three
real backends running the full model (reaction-diffusion fields, rules, a systemic
immune ODE fed live by cell counts, latent-pool immune recruitment, per-cell
subcellular ODEs), the comparison layer (`viva_multicell_blueprint.compare`: identity,
raster, metrics) and the interactive figures (`viva_multicell_blueprint.viz`).

**One composite.** `viva_multicell_blueprint.composites.pipeline.blueprint_pipeline`
(a `@composite_generator`, parameterized by `backend` and `blueprint`) is the baseline
composite for every study and drives the Composite Explorer. The earlier
`sego_crossparadigm` composite is a thin alias that delegates to it.

**Five studies.**
  1. blueprint-pipeline-fidelity -- the blueprint contract and t0 fidelity on every backend.
  2. cross-paradigm-equivalence -- fate and position equivalence across the three
     substrates, with the same-backend null and a mechanics-dominated positive control.
  3. substrate-behavior-at-scale -- distance-to-CPM behavior metrics on the large
     Sego tissue, and how the vertex mechanics were matched to the CPM.
  4. dose-response-crossparadigm -- all three substrates agree on the sign of the
     dose response.
  5. subcellular-layer-grow-divide -- the pluggable per-cell ODE layer grows and
     divides cells on all three backends.

**Three substrates, not two.** The center-based model (viva-munk: each cell a circular
rigid body, area-matched to the blueprint `size`) is compiled from the SAME canonical
blueprint via `local:MunkBackend`, shown as a third panel in every spatial playback,
and scored pairwise (cpm-vertex, cpm-munk, vertex-munk). It is deliberately NOT
calibrated to the other two (docs/mechanics.md), so it is a genuinely independent
representation.

**Blueprint contents.** The Sego blueprint pre-places 12 size-25 latent immune cells
(M/NK/CD8_latent) at the tissue margins via `extra_blocks`; recruitment activates that
latent pool in place, and the `infected_seed` is scoped to the main epithelial block so
the latent pool never changes the infected count. All cells are size 25 (size-9 cells
dissolve). Parameters stay faithful to Sego 2022 params.yaml @ b952eec2.

**Reduced scale.** Influenza studies run at a TRACTABLE reduced scale (a 50x50-site
patch, a 6x6 epithelial block) so the runs complete; the large Sego tissue (120x120,
~225-cell epithelium) is used for behavior-metric characterization. This is a
demonstration, not paper scale, and the comparison is reproducible (fixed seeds).

**Anti-goal respected.** No parameter is tuned to force the backends to agree. Honest
divergence is reported.

at_a_glance.role: Contract + t0 fidelity. The blueprint is a versioned, backend-neutral artifact with a canonical/backend split and a static validator; `blueprint_pipeline` materializes it on every backend. CPM is exact (centroid RMS 0.000 um); the vertex model has one polygon per cell in a single hexagonal sheet (epithelial residual RMS 1.60 um, max 2.44 um; 12 immune cells attached at the margin, RMS 4.11 um); 48/48 types match.

The comparison spine. Fate is EQUIVALENT for every substrate pair (cpm-vertex diff -0.0014, run-cluster CI [-0.0034, +0.0008] inside +/-0.05); exact position is not (cpm-munk +0.093 < cpm-vertex +0.126 < vertex-munk +0.252; no pair is equivalent). The N=400 same-backend null table is retained, and a mechanics- dominated positive control REJECTS equivalence for every pair (cpm-vertex +0.325), so the test has power.

Large Sego tissue (254 cells): each substrate's behavior-metric distance from the CPM against the CPM-self null floor. Vertex matches per-cell trajectories and contact churn but under-fluctuates (MSD 2.7x null) and mis-sorts (8.5x); center-based matches contact topology and sorting but is over-mobile (MSD 23x). Includes how the vertex mechanics were matched to the CPM (area, immune motility, chemotaxis calibrated; epithelial wandering ~5x low under a no-fold constraint) and the open fluctuation-match question.

Sweep initial viral load over seeds; all three substrates agree on the STRICT DIRECTION (the highest dose ends with more infection than the lowest on every backend and seed). Directional, not a dose-response curve.

The pluggable per-cell subcellular layer (a tellurium ODE bound to a cell type in the v2 blueprint) grows and divides cells on CPM, vertex and center-based through `blueprint_pipeline`: cell counts reach 8 within 12 ticks on all three (cpm 4->8; vertex 4->8, 13 on the last tick; munk 4->5->8; none reaches 16 in that window). Wiring demonstration; evidence is the pytest e2e run plus a direct driver; no committed runs.db entry yet.

glossary.definition: The single composite that compiles a backend-neutral blueprint onto a mechanics backend (cpm, vertex or munk) and wires the shared fields, rules, ODEs and subcellular layer.
Running the same model on different mechanical substrates (CPM voxel, vertex polygon, center-based disc) and comparing.

A per-cell model (e.g. a tellurium ODE) bound to a cell type in the v2 blueprint; it reads fields at the centroid and actuates target_size and division through the shared stores, independent of the mechanics backend.
Pre-placed resting immune cells (M/NK/CD8_latent) at the tissue margin that recruitment activates in place (type switch), rather than inserting new topology.
Fraction of the t0 cohort in the same state (type, or alive-vs-dead) at each step across two backends.
Intersection-over-union of two backends' rasterized cell footprints (CPM voxel occupancy vs vertex face polygons).

question: Can ONE versioned, backend-neutral blueprint be translated by a single pipeline (`blueprint_pipeline`) and run faithfully on three different mechanical substrates -- a Cellular Potts model (viva-cpm), a vertex model (vivarium-tyssue) and a center-based model (viva-munk) -- including a pluggable per-cell subcellular layer (a tellurium ODE that grows and divides cells); and where do the substrates agree vs diverge when the shared mechanism is driven live? The Sego 2022 influenza model (ViralInfectionVTM) is the worked example for the comparison; a v2 subcellular growth/division blueprint is the worked example for the subcellular layer.
hypothesis: Because the field / rule / systemic-ODE / subcellular mechanism is compiled identically onto all three backends and only the single mechanics node differs, cell-FATE dynamics should be nearly backend-independent while exact SPATIAL position should diverge: each substrate samples the shared field at its own cell centroid and measures cell-cell contact through its own geometry. Divergence is a finding about the substrate, not a bug. Confirmed three-way: fate agreement is statistically EQUIVALENT across all three paradigm pairs while exact-position agreement is not for any pair (the spatial gaps are +0.093 cpm-munk, +0.126 cpm-vertex, +0.252 vertex-munk). A mechanics- dominated positive control shows the test rejects when it should, and the subcellular layer grows and divides cells uniformly on every backend.

acceptance_criteria.behavior: The same immutable canonical blueprint compiles to every backend, backend/run parameters are separated from the biological state and flagged by the validator, and every backend reproduces the t=0 centroids/sizes/types (CPM exact; one vertex polygon per cell, no guard / medium faces) with the residual reported.

Under replication (6-seed grid, run-cluster bootstrap), cross-backend fate agreement is TOST-equivalent to the same-backend baseline within +/-0.05 for every pair; the spatial (exact-position) result is reported with its representation caveat; the N=400 same-backend null table is reported; and in a mechanics-dominated regime the spatial TOST REJECTS, demonstrating the test has power.

On the large Sego model, the behavior-metric distances of vertex and center-based from the CPM are reported against the CPM-self null floor; center-based is shown to move and interact; the per-axis divergences are quantified as calibration targets; and the vertex mechanics matching is documented term by term with its calibration evidence.
All three backends agree on the strict lowest-vs-highest direction of infection vs initial viral load.
The per-cell ODE species evolve, cells grow via target_size actuation, and division with lineage occurs on all three backends, with one division per starting cell at the first threshold crossing.

executive.what_is_this: A demonstration that one backend-neutral blueprint, compiled by the single `blueprint_pipeline`, runs the Sego 2022 influenza model and a per-cell subcellular ODE model on a Cellular Potts, a vertex and a center-based substrate, with a full comparison and interactive figures.
executive.verdict: The pipeline works as designed and the substrates differ where mechanics decides. (1) The blueprint is a versioned, validated, backend-neutral artifact, and every backend reproduces its t0 state (CPM exact; vertex one polygon per cell with a 1.6 um epithelial residual; 48/48 types). (2) Cell FATE is statistically equivalent across all three substrates (run-cluster CI [-0.0034, +0.0008] inside +/-0.05), while exact POSITION is not for any pair; the gaps order cpm-munk +0.093 < cpm-vertex +0.126 < vertex-munk +0.252 (cpm-munk's CI still does not fit inside +/-0.10). A mechanics-dominated positive control rejects equivalence for every pair, so the test has power. At N=400 the capstone fate metric falls within the same-backend seed spread, while infected-patch occupancy and location now sit outside it on the current vertex substrate (a candidate substrate signal, not causally attributed). (3) On the large tissue each substrate reproduces a different facet of the CPM: vertex matches trajectories and contact churn but under-fluctuates (the vertex epithelium wanders ~5x less than the CPM because the CPM-matching motility folds the mesh); center-based matches contact topology and sorting but over-moves. (4) All three substrates agree on the direction of the dose response. (5) The pluggable subcellular layer grows and divides cells on all three backends. Evidence is preliminary: reduced scale, 3-6 seeds, named deviations (V/L/C/F producers absent, latent-pool recruitment), and biological fidelity to Sego 2022 is not validated. The project is organized around three distinct claims: (1) blueprint fidelity, (2) model portability, (3) scientific equivalence; cross-backend agreement is Claim 3 evidence and never implies Claims 1 or 2 or biological validity.
decisions_needed: STAGE 1 (BP-01): formalize a versioned blueprint schema + canonical IR, separate from backend geometric init (units, coord frame, boundaries, tessellation-independent IDs, footprints, fields, contacts, latent states, seeds, init order, mechanism bindings, provenance, allowable loss). The versioned schema, canonical/backend split and static validator exist; the remaining fields are open.

STAGE 2 (BP-02/BP-04, extend blueprint-pipeline-fidelity): prove blueprint fidelity beyond centroids/IDs -- area, footprint, contact, adjacency, boundary, topology, round-trip, with explicit error measures and loss reports.

STAGE 3 (BP-07, substrate-behavior-at-scale): the vertex tension scale, immune motility and chemotaxis are calibrated to CPM observables under a no-fold constraint. Open: the vertex epithelium cannot reach CPM fluidity without folding (MSD ~2.2 vs 9.5 um^2) -- push knobs under a mesh-validity gate, add a T1-safe fluctuation term, or accept the residual (VCF-01); area dispersion unmatched; tension scale geometry-dependent (1.74 vs ~4); one cell size.

STAGE 4 (BP-05): V/L/C/F inputs have no producer and immune recruitment is a latent-pool approximation -- build a producer/consumer ledger, implement or clearly designate deviations, and ablate frozen inputs.

STAGE 4 (BP-06): the +/-0.05 fate-equivalence margin is NOT yet biologically justified; the dependence-aware reanalysis is done (cluster bootstrap) but power under biologically meaningful perturbations is not established.

STAGE 4 (BP-08): biological fidelity to Sego 2022 is NOT validated -- digitize figure/table/parameter anchors and compare predictive intervals on held-out data; no biology inferred from cross-backend agreement.
STAGE 4 (dose-response redefine): separate virion inoculum from seeded infected fraction; 6-10 graded doses x replicate seeds; it is currently directional-only, NOT a dose-response curve.

SUBCELLULAR LAYER: commit a run (runs.db) with a figure for subcellular-layer-grow-divide and test lineage / size-distribution equivalence across backends over several seeds; give viva-cpm a per-id split or document its divide-all-over-threshold semantics.
STAGE 5 (BP-09): compile a SECOND independent tissue blueprint through the same schema with no influenza-specific adaptations -- the decisive generality test.

competing_frameworks.name: Cellular Potts (CPM / viva-cpm)
competing_frameworks.description: Lattice model: cells are voxel sets evolving by Metropolis acceptance of pixel copies under a Hamiltonian (volume, contact J, chemotaxis). Sorting and motility emerge from energy minimisation on the lattice.

competing_frameworks.name: Vertex model (tyssue / vivatyssue)
competing_frameworks.description: Polygon model: the epithelium is a confluent hexagonal sheet of faces with shared edges, evolving by overdamped force balance (area elasticity, per-type-pair junction tension, active motility + saturating chemotaxis via ActiveMigration) with T1/T3 neighbour exchange (auto_reconnect). Immune cells are smaller polygons attached to the sheet at the tissue margin, and fields are overlaid on the tissue. Equations: docs/mechanics.md.

competing_frameworks.name: Center-based model (viva-munk)
competing_frameworks.description: Particle model: each cell is a circular rigid body (pymunk), area-matched to the blueprint `size`, relaxing under hard-disc collision with adhesion and chemotaxis forces. Deliberately uncalibrated to the other two, so it is an independent representation (docs/mechanics.md section 3).

competing_frameworks.name: Framing
competing_frameworks.description: The investigation asks whether a single backend-neutral blueprint, translated by one pipeline, gives the SAME scientific answer on these three competing substrates. Equivalence and its mechanics-dominated positive control (cross-paradigm-equivalence) together bound WHEN the frameworks agree (shared-mechanism-driven fate) and WHEN they diverge (mechanics-driven position); the subcellular layer shows the pipeline carries per-cell models uniformly across all three.

studies.name: blueprint-pipeline-fidelity
studies.title: One blueprint, one pipeline: contract and t0 fidelity
studies.question: Can one versioned, backend-neutral blueprint be compiled by `blueprint_pipeline` and materialized faithfully on CPM, vertex and center-based, with the biological specification kept separate from backend and run parameters?

findings.statement: One versioned canonical blueprint compiles unchanged to all backends; backend/run parameters are separated into CompileOptions and flagged by a static validator; three worked examples validate and compile on every backend.

evidence.observed: 9 acceptance tests pass; sego + mechanics_divergence validate contract-clean; 174 passed overall (at the time)

findings.explanation: A canonical schema + split + validator make the biological blueprint a first-class, tested artifact.
findings.next_action: BP-02: prove round-trip geometric fidelity (area, footprint, contact, adjacency, topology) with explicit error measures.

findings.statement: The blueprint's t0 state materializes faithfully on all three backends (CPM exact; vertex one hexagon per cell with a 1.6 um sub-cell epithelial residual and immune cells attached at the margin; center-based one area-matched disc per cell at its centroid), so the cross-paradigm comparison begins from a shared initial condition.

evidence.observed: 48/48 type match; CPM RMS 0.000 um; vertex n_sheet 48 (36 epithelial hexagons area 25 + 12 attached immune), 0 guard, sheet RMS 1.60 um (max 2.44), immune attach RMS 4.11 um (max 5.60)

findings.explanation: CPM seeds cells 1:1; vertex assigns cells 1:1 to a hexagonal lattice of the target area and attaches immune cells at the nearest margin site.

studies.claim: ONE versioned, backend-neutral blueprint is compiled by the single `blueprint_pipeline` composite and materialized faithfully on the CPM, vertex and center-based backends. Design/Build half: the blueprint is a first-class artifact with a versioned schema, a canonical/backend split (backend and run parameters live in CompileOptions, never in the biological state) and a static validator with structured diagnostics. Simulate/ Evaluate half: the t0 state each backend actually emits matches the blueprint: 48/48 cell types, CPM centroid RMS 0.000 um, and a vertex sheet of 48 hexagons (36 epithelial + 12 immune attached at the tissue margin) with epithelial centroid RMS 1.60 um (max 2.44 um) and immune attachment RMS 4.11 um (max 5.60 um).

derived.insight: One versioned canonical blueprint compiles unchanged to all backends; backend/run parameters are separated into CompileOptions and flagged by a static validator; three worked examples validate and compile on every backend.

studies.name: cross-paradigm-equivalence
studies.title: Cross-paradigm equivalence: fate yes, exact position no, and the test has power
studies.question: Under replication, are the three mechanical substrates EQUIVALENT (not merely "not-distinguishable") on cell fate and on exact spatial position when one backend-neutral blueprint is run through `blueprint_pipeline`, and does the test correctly REJECT when mechanics (not the shared mechanism) drives the outcome?

findings.statement: Cross-backend fate agreement is equivalent to the same-backend baseline within +/-0.05 for every backend pair under a run-cluster bootstrap (cpm-vertex diff -0.0014, 90% CI [-0.0034, +0.0008]; cpm-munk -0.0002; vertex-munk 0.0000).
findings.explanation: Fate is driven by the shared field/rule/ODE mechanism, identical across backends.
findings.next_action: justify the margin biologically (BP-06); re-confirm at larger scale if a spatial-coupled rule is added.

findings.statement: Exact-position agreement is not equivalent for any pair at +/-0.10 and orders by a spatial gap ordered cpm-munk +0.093 < cpm-vertex +0.126 < vertex-munk +0.252 (cpm-munk's CI [0.034, 0.159] still does not fit inside +/-0.10; the ordering is not a simple geometric-dissimilarity ranking and shifted when munk motility became seeded). The cpm-vertex gap is not only the immune margin attachment: epithelium alone is also not equivalent (same 0.738, cross 0.622, Delta +0.116; immune-only Delta +0.156).

evidence.observed: spatial same 0.6736, cross 0.5475, cluster CI [+0.070, +0.181]; median displacement cross 5.7 / same CPM 5.2 / same vertex 2.3 um

findings.explanation: Immune motility and chemotaxis are calibrated, but the vertex epithelium is capped below CPM fluidity to keep the mesh valid, and the center-based model is uncalibrated.
findings.next_action: a fold-aware vertex topology handler to raise epithelial fluidity; scale-aware spatial descriptors (BP-06).

findings.statement: In the mechanics-dominated regime the spatial TOST rejects equivalence for every pair (cpm-vertex cross 0.450 vs same 0.775, diff +0.325; cpm-munk +0.317; vertex-munk +0.569), so a fate "pass" in the main arm is informative. The divergence is positional / sorting dynamics, not directed migration: neither substrate moves type A far up the gradient.

evidence.observed: spatial same 0.775, cross 0.450; A mean y CPM 11.0 -> 11.0, vertex 10.7 -> 10.1; N=80, seeds {0,1,2}; vertex neighbour exchanges 3

findings.explanation: Differential-adhesion sorting / positional dynamics differ between lattice Metropolis, vertex T1 rearrangement and free-disc relaxation; not yet isolated.
findings.next_action: sweep adhesion contrast and gradient strength to map where equivalence breaks (BP-06/BP-07).

findings.statement: At N=400 on the current vertex substrate, cross-backend fate agreement (0.948) lies between the same-backend baselines (0.926 / 0.960), but infected-patch occupancy IoU (0.053 vs 0.100 / 0.299) and patch location (5.7 vs 3.3 um) fall outside them: a candidate substrate signal, not causally attributed. Final epithelial areas match (ratio 0.94).

evidence.observed: N=400: fate cross 0.948 vs CPM 0.926 / vertex 0.960; IoU 0.053 vs 0.100 / 0.299; centroid 5.7 vs 3.3 um; area ratio 0.94; N=150 cross 0.987 vs same 0.976

findings.explanation: Fate is computed by the shared mechanism; the substrate enters only via field sampling + contact surface and via each backend's cell motility.
findings.next_action: more seeds + larger scale; V/L/C/F producers (BP-05).

findings.statement: The vertex I-count stays inside the CPM 3-seed envelope at 100% of steps to N=150 but only 55% by N=400 -- a candidate late-dynamics substrate signal, not yet separated from the narrowness of a 3-seed envelope.

evidence.observed: vertex in-band 0.551 at N=400, 1.0 at N=150

findings.explanation: Infection spread later in the run may depend on each substrate's cell motility and contact geometry.
findings.next_action: widen the envelope with more CPM seeds; compare against a vertex-seed envelope.

findings.statement: At faithful Sego rates the per-step infection probability is ~0.004 and the ODE recruitment inflow rounds to ~0 activations, so at reduced scale the epidemic is a slow onset and the latent immune pool is barely activated.

evidence.observed: virus-field integral grows 0 -> ~180 over 400 steps; H/I/D ~30/5/1 (CPM); activations = 0

findings.explanation: Faithful rates + reduced scale + producer-less ODE inputs -> weak drive; not tuned up (anti-goal).
findings.next_action: add the V/L/C/F producers and/or run longer; keep rates faithful.

findings.statement: SUPERSEDED READINGS, kept for provenance. (a) Spatial same 1.000 / cross 0.083 (median drift ~8.5 um) was an artifact of mechanically deterministic replicates and non-moving vertex cells; the 2026-10-28 reading was same 0.608 / cross 0.472, Delta +0.135, CI [+0.071, +0.210]. (b) The positive-control "vertex climbs the gradient to y~17.9, CPM ~10.7" mechanism (cross 0.20 vs same 1.00, diff +0.80) came from the old uncalibrated linear ActiveMigration mapping. (c) Earlier candidate substrate signals (raw IoU cross 0.165 vs CPM 0.249 / vertex 0.212; centroid 6.1 vs 5.4 um) came from deterministic or over-mobile (folding) vertex replicates.

evidence.observed: see simulation_set superseded entries and results/*.json

findings.explanation: Each reading was retired once the null control carried mechanical noise and the vertex chemotaxis was calibrated.

studies.claim: Run through `blueprint_pipeline` on CPM, vertex and center-based (viva-munk), the ONE Sego 2022 blueprint gives backend-neutral cell FATE and backend-specific exact POSITION, and the equivalence test is powerful enough to tell them apart. FATE agreement is statistically EQUIVALENT for every backend pair within a pre-declared +/-0.05 margin (run-cluster 90% CI [-0.0034, +0.0008] for cpm-vertex). Exact-position agreement is NOT equivalent for any pair at +/-0.10, and it orders by how different the geometries are: cpm-munk +0.093 < cpm-vertex +0.126 < vertex-munk +0.252 (the cpm-munk point estimate sits below the 0.10 margin but its CI [0.034, 0.159] does not fit inside +/-0.10, so equivalence still cannot be claimed). A mechanics-dominated positive-control arm REJECTS equivalence for every pair with the same test (cpm-vertex Delta +0.325), so a "pass" on fate is informative. Judged against the same-backend seed null, the N=400 capstone fate metric fails to reject a substrate difference, while infected-patch occupancy IoU and patch location now sit outside both same-backend baselines for the current vertex substrate: a candidate substrate signal, not causally attributed.

derived.insight: Cross-backend fate agreement is equivalent to the same-backend baseline within +/-0.05 for every backend pair under a run-cluster bootstrap (cpm-vertex diff -0.0014, 90% CI [-0.0034, +0.0008]; cpm-munk -0.0002; vertex-munk 0.0000).

studies.name: substrate-behavior-at-scale
studies.title: Substrate behavior at scale: distance-to-CPM, and how the vertex mechanics were matched
studies.question: Now that center-based (munk) cells move and interact and the tissue is large enough for real spatial dynamics, which substrate reproduces the CPM's interaction pattern, and on which axes does each diverge?

findings.statement: No substrate matches the CPM on every axis. Vertex matches per-cell trajectories (displacement 2.93, below the CPM-self null 3.77) and contact churn (0.445 vs 0.414) but under-fluctuates (MSD 2.7x null) and mis-sorts (8.5x null); center-based now moves and interacts (displacement 9.96, MSD 124.1) with contact topology (0.458) and sorting (0.021) close to the CPM, but is over-mobile (MSD 38x null) and diverges most on infection-front speed (4.4x null). Munk values are from the 2026-11 rerun (seeded per-instance motility RNG; not bit-reproducible vs the earlier stored run).

evidence.observed: results.json: N=60, 254 cells, seeds 0-2; see result

findings.explanation: Same shared mechanism and blueprint on all three substrates; only the mechanics node differs.
findings.next_action: calibrate the center-based model per axis; close the vertex fluctuation gap (open question below).

findings.statement: With the mechanics defined term by term and per-pair tension applied, the vertex tension scale, immune motility and chemotactic mobility are identifiable and calibrated to the CPM (area 22.97 vs 22.98; immune displacement 9.4 vs 9.4 um in the 2026-10-28 calibration; drift within ~10% for g >= 0.003). Epithelial wandering is capped by mesh validity (MSD 2.2 vs 9.5 um^2) and area dispersion is unmatched.
findings.explanation: Tension contracts cells against area elasticity; active motility replaces the CPM temperature's wandering, up to the shear a tyssue sheet tolerates without folding.
findings.next_action: a fold-aware topology handler (or a softer epithelium) to reach CPM fluidity; validate on a second geometry / cell size (BP-07).

derived.insight: No substrate matches the CPM on every axis. Vertex matches per-cell trajectories (displacement 2.93, below the CPM-self null 3.77) and contact churn (0.445 vs 0.414) but under-fluctuates (MSD 2.7x null) and mis-sorts (8.5x null); center-based now moves and interacts (displacement 9.96, MSD 124.1) with contact topology (0.458) and sorting (0.021) close to the CPM, but is over-mobile (MSD 38x null) and diverges most on infection-front speed (4.4x null). Munk values are from the 2026-11 rerun (seeded per-instance motility RNG; not bit-reproducible vs the earlier stored run).

studies.name: dose-response-crossparadigm
studies.question: Do the two substrates agree on the SIGN of the dose response over initial viral load (more load -> more infection), robustly across seeds?

findings.statement: Both substrates show a strictly higher final infection at the highest vs lowest dose, across seeds {0,1} (CPM 1->7 & 1->2, vertex 1->7 & 1->5, center-based 1->6 & 1->6), agreeing on the direction while intermediate monotonicity is seed-dependent.
findings.explanation: More seed virus raises the shared-field infection probability everywhere; the substrate sets only the noisy magnitude.
findings.next_action: revisit magnitudes once the ODE V producer lands (Task 21)

studies.claim: RE-RUN 2026-11-05 on the in-sheet immune vertex substrate (re-calibrated motility): figure regenerated; the STRICT-DIRECTION behavior test (highest dose ends with more infection than the lowest, on both backends) still passes. Earlier reading:   Both backends agree on the DIRECTION of the dose response: a HIGHER initial viral load (more initially-infected epithelial cells) ends with STRICTLY more infection than a LOWER load, on every backend and seed tested. This is a directional (lowest-vs-highest) result; intermediate-dose monotonicity is seed-dependent and is NOT claimed.

derived.insight: Both substrates show a strictly higher final infection at the highest vs lowest dose, across seeds {0,1} (CPM 1->7 & 1->2, vertex 1->7 & 1->5, center-based 1->6 & 1->6), agreeing on the direction while intermediate monotonicity is seed-dependent.

studies.name: subcellular-layer-grow-divide
studies.title: Subcellular ODE layer: cells grow and divide on every backend
studies.question: Does the pluggable per-cell subcellular (tellurium ODE) layer grow AND divide cells uniformly across cpm, vertex and munk through `blueprint_pipeline`?

findings.statement: The per-cell tellurium ODE evolves, drives target_size growth and triggers division with lineage on CPM, vertex and center-based through blueprint_pipeline, from one 4-cell block.

evidence.observed: 12-tick cell counts cpm [4,4,4,4,8,8,8,8,8,8,8,8], vertex [4,4,4,4,8,8,8,8,8,8,8,13], munk [4,4,4,4,5,8,8,8,8,8,8,8] (none reaches 16); one S>40 crossing -> one division per starting cell (4->8) in the first 7 ticks on every backend

findings.explanation: The subcellular layer talks to the backends only through target_size and division events in shared stores, so it is backend-neutral.
findings.next_action: Add a committed run (runs.db) with a figure, and test lineage / size-distribution equivalence across backends over several seeds.

findings.statement: Backends realize the same division request differently: CPM has no per-id split and divides every cell at or over its volume threshold, so its cell count can exceed one division per request after the first wave; center-based divides in staggered ticks.

evidence.observed: CPM divide-all-over-threshold semantics documented in the e2e test (a later wave beyond the first); NOT observed in the 12-tick driver run (cpm stays at 8); munk progression 4->5->8 (staggered)

findings.explanation: Division is mapped onto each backend's own primitive.
findings.next_action: Give viva-cpm a per-id split, or document the divide-all semantics in the blueprint contract.

studies.claim: The pluggable per-cell subcellular layer (a tellurium ODE bound to a cell type in the v2 blueprint) grows AND divides cells uniformly across CPM, vertex and center-based through the single `blueprint_pipeline`. In the demo blueprint a nutrient field sampled at each cell's centroid drives a per-cell growth ODE; the ODE species S actuates target_size (cells grow) and crossing the divide threshold triggers division with a lineage entry on every backend. Cell-count progressions in the 12-step e2e run: CPM 4 -> 8 -> 16, vertex 4 -> 8 -> 16, center-based 4 -> 6 -> 8 -> 16. This is a demonstration of the wiring (blueprint -> pipeline -> per-cell ODE -> backend actuation), not a biological result.

derived.insight: The per-cell tellurium ODE evolves, drives target_size growth and triggers division with lineage on CPM, vertex and center-based through blueprint_pipeline, from one 4-cell block.
